entity.name: Bradley Slimp
entity.description: Independent researcher and software maintainer building open-source AI governance infrastructure. Creator of BiasClear and the Persistent Influence Theory (PIT) framework, published on SSRN and Zenodo with a DOI. BiasClear is maintained as a solo public-interest project without institutional backing.

projects.name: BiasClear
projects.description: BiasClear is open-source structural persuasion detection infrastructure for the AI ecosystem. It audits text for rhetorical manipulation patterns such as manufactured consensus, authority substitution, false urgency, and dissent dismissal—patterns that sentiment, toxicity, and fact-checking tools do not target well. The system combines a deterministic frozen core of 42 hand-authored detection patterns across legal, media, financial, and general domains with governed LLM-assisted analysis, SHA-256 hash-chained auditability, and a live public deployment at biasclear.com. Funding would support validation, independent security review, and broader adoption of this public-interest governance layer.

plans.name: Validation and external audit
plans.description: Funds calibration corpus expansion, external annotation, reproducible evaluation, and an independent security review. This is the highest-leverage step for moving BiasClear from an early production artifact to a stronger public reference tool.

plans.name: Infrastructure and maintenance
plans.description: Supports hosting, compute, CI, documentation, and ongoing maintenance of the live public API and open-source codebase so BiasClear remains available to researchers, reviewers, and downstream integrators.
